# How it works today: Larkspur Ceramics

1. [MEDIUM E-06] A purchase order arrives as a PDF attachment, never in the email body.
2. [HIGH E-01, E-02] The order coordinator types each line into the shared order sheet; customers write the same product code several ways (LC-1204, lc1204, 1204-LC, 1204LC).
3. [MEDIUM E-08] At the end of the day the bookkeeper types the day's orders into QuickBooks Online; nobody confirms an order until then, sometimes the next day.
4. [HIGH E-03, E-07] Every Monday the order coordinator corrects the product codes in the sheet by hand.
5. [LOW E-09] The typing takes about two hours a day (suggested by Robin, the client agreed).
6. [MEDIUM E-12] The studio shop's point-of-sale system can list each sale's line items by product code through its API; research only, so MEDIUM: it shows what the vendor documents, not what the shop's own account does.

## Where it breaks
- [HIGH E-01] One product code in four forms in a single month's sheet.
- [UNKNOWN] How many orders a normal week holds (60 or 90). Who can answer: operations manager.
